page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula of borax
lines: decahydrate. The 10H₂O is its water of
It is a white crystalline solid.
steps.why: The question asks for one formula, so the formula itself is the answer, and giving the chemical name in the same breath shows that the ten water molecules are part of the crystal rather than an impurity.
common_mistakes: Writing Na₂B₄O₇ alone. Borax is the decahydrate, so the 10H₂O belongs in the formula.
Writing three boron atoms. Borax has four, in B₄O₇.
steps.memory_tip: Read the subscripts in order: two sodium, four boron, seven oxygen, ten water.
steps.margin_note: Write the dot before 10H₂O. It separates the water of crystallisation from the salt.

steps.label: The tetranuclear form
steps.mark_note: The chemical name or the tetranuclear form
lines: Both forms have the same atoms and both
are correct. Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O is the form
steps.why: Both formulas count to two sodium, four boron, seventeen oxygen and twenty hydrogen atoms, so a student who meets the bracketed form in a textbook should recognise it as the same borax.
common_mistakes: Treating Na₂[B₄O₅(OH)₄]·8H₂O as a different compound. It is the same borax.
Writing 10H₂O with the bracketed form. Two of the ten water molecules are used up in building the four OH groups, so eight are left.
steps.memory_tip: Four OH groups plus eight waters give the same twenty hydrogen atoms as ten waters.
steps.margin_note: Write the familiar formula first, then add the bracketed form if there is room.

insider_note: The answer is one line of formula, so use the rest of the space on the chemical name and the water of crystallisation instead of extra sentences.
